population: the 3,549 rows of the C32 sweep that still diverge on the current build (fingerprint 51d56b3f, 53 patches, post-C34), of which 515 are unattributed
how_the_population_was_built: Re-read all 7,249 retained C32 rows through the CURRENT build with cert_sweep_reread.reread_row, then re-derived divergence_class with the differential's own classify_divergence. Validation: this reproduces the C34 postmeasure exactly -- 515 unattributed = 433 structural + 37 same_turn + 36 generic + 9 truant -- so the offline instrument agrees with the sweep readout.

question_1_the_crit_hypothesis.claim_tested: the 37 same_turn_stat_event_gap rows are unpriced crits, which would move them to the engine-gap bucket beside C27 and C31

evidence.note: the deciding pair is the one the rule actually inspects: the first miss with exactly one observed and one engine component whose ratio falls in [0.70, 0.96]

question_1_the_crit_hypothesis.why_the_earlier_reading_was_wrong: TWO independent errors, either one fatal. (1) POPULATION: I measured over all 7,249 retained rows, which carry no divergence_class field -- so attribute_row took cls='' and every row fell through to UNATTRIBUTED. The measurement was not mis-scoped, it was invalid at the root. (2) PAIR: I averaged over every component pair on the arm rather than the pair the rule inspects. The rule fires on observed SMALLER than engine (0.70-0.96); a 2x crit ratio cannot trigger it, which the arithmetic said plainly before any measurement did.
question_1_the_crit_hypothesis.the_correlation_that_misled_me: 24 of the 37 protocols DO contain |-crit|. Crits are present at these boundaries -- they are just not what the rule is complaining about. A true signal on the boundary is not evidence for a claim about the pair.

question_2_what_is_actually_wrong.finding: 32 of 37 rows are decided by a MINORITY arm, not the majority arm.
question_2_what_is_actually_wrong.this_is_the_C28_defect_at_a_second_site: C28 scoped the roll_scaled_component rule to the majority arm for exactly this reason -- a small-mass branch was deciding rows whose majority arm a documented family already explained (22 of 29 structural rows on the 52-patch build). The same-turn rule has the identical shape and was never scoped. I4's words apply unchanged: a tie confined to a minority arm cannot explain the majority-arm complaint.
question_2_what_is_actually_wrong.bucket: instrument-artifact -- the engine's arm is not wrong here, the rule is reading the wrong arm

registered_prediction.change: scope the same-turn boost/status rule in scripts/cert_sweep_readout.py attribute_row to the majority arm only, matching C28's scoping of roll_scaled_component
registered_prediction.identity_level_falsifier: Counts matching is NOT sufficient -- C29 passed its count check and failed its identity check. These 32 named rows must move, to these named families, and the 5 named rows must stay. Any substitution falsifies the prediction even at equal counts.
registered_prediction.does_not_reach_a_pass: 485 unattributed against a required zero. This closes one shape, not the sweep.

appendix_x_bar: This verdict REDUCES the residue by 30 rows, so under X.3.3 it carries the higher bar rather than the permissive one. The bar is met by the identity-level falsifier above plus the precedent: the identical correction was made, measured and validated at the roll_scaled_component site in C28.
era_consequence: This edits the readout, so readout_sha256 changes and the matcher era advances. Every limit adjudication must be mechanically re-derived against the new era before the audit table can be read as current -- that is the rule, not a courtesy.
